purpose: Test whether clearing stale scaling suffix entries and rebuilding factors only for the exported active NLP improves the IDAES 2.12 solve trajectory.
interpretation: The active-only rebuild removes all writer warnings but produces a catastrophic first step and is much worse than the retained whole-model AutoScaler control.
Skipped stale or non-exportable scaling suffix entries are not the cause of the modern convergence failure.

Some distinction between the inherited/whole-model policy and a uniform active-row Jacobian-norm policy is numerically important; likely candidates include treatment of inequalities and inherited constraint factors.
The active-NLP path remains opt-in for reproducible diagnostics and is not recommended as the modernization scaling policy.
